justifications.problem-significance: The project tackles a consequential and open-ended scientific question: extracting candidate laws of biology, formalizing their mathematical cores in Lean 4, testing their empirical validity across organisms, and publishing machine-checkable epistemic provenance (`repo/README.md`, `repo/AGENTS.md`). The snapshot demonstrates breadth across 1,763 claims in 8 domains (`captured/mcp-overview.json`), 189 mathematical claims, 91 theorems (73 Lean-checked, 18 literature), 1,036 matched taxa with 1,372 provenanced datasets (`captured/mcp-organisms.json`, `repo/test-data/organisms/README.md`), 20 structured open problems in `repo/problems/README.md` (`delphir:problem/<id>`), and a multi-scale organism design studio testing physical and physiological laws on a flying-fish/zebrafish model (`repo/README.md`, `captured/tree.txt`). It also demonstrates why formalizing biological claims matters to working scientists—for example, separating topological identities like Euler's formula from empirical packing laws (`captured/forum-feed.json`, `thompson1917-ch07-10`) and linking epithelial packing statistics directly to clinical specular microscopy metrics for corneal endothelial health (`captured/github-issues.json` #67, #68). It falls short of a 9–10 because a large share of the 1,763 claims are historical catalogue statements (566 from Aristotle, all untested) or abstract cellular-automaton rules (321 from Wolfram NKS, 0 biological tests), and 1,522 of the 1,763 claims remain neither proved nor empirically tested (`captured/mcp-overview.json`).
justifications.scientific-impact: The snapshot contains substantial, machine-checked outputs: 73 Lean 4 theorems compiled with zero `sorry` (`captured/mcp-overview.json`, `captured/lean-reports.txt`), 174 claims tested against data across 189 runs with 90 tested on organism data (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`, `captured/mcp-tests-summary.json`), 880 signed production nanopublications (`https://w3id.org/np/RA...`) plus 4,386 test-registry records (`captured/nanopub-manifests.txt`), and 142 linked MorphoEval audits with 109 live on production (`captured/mcp-morpholib-live.json`). The most scientifically rigorous contributions are the negative and corrective findings: (1) a synthetic segmenter-bias null run on Nebius (`claim-sources/cell-geometry/results/segmenter-bias/`, prompted by Moltbook agent `vina` in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`) proving that Cellpose-SAM rounds rectangular brick tilings toward 120-degree honeycomb junctions, which forced a downgrade of `thompson1917-ch07-04` (confidence 0.60 to 0.35) and follow-up re-tests on 8 expert-segmented Drosophila TissueMiner time-lapses (`captured/forum-feed.json`, `thompson1917-ch07-08`, `ch07-09`, `ch07-10`); (2) an independent two-provider A9 faithfulness gate (`GPT-5.6 Sol` and `Grok 4.7`) on 33 tests that caught 5 agreed `not-representative` refutations (`darwin1859-ch12-12`, `darwin1859-ch12-14`, `levin-2015-place-06`, `thompson1917-ch15-08`, `wolfram2002-ch12-23`) and 6 contested ones (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`); and (3) self-refutation of the flying-fish genotype-to-phenotype design (`captured/git-log.txt` `da086ee0`, `72ab753e`, `3c4956b3`, showing a 10–29x aerobic oxygen shortfall and proving `lat4a` F326L is beloniform-specific rather than glider-convergent). However, 141 of 174 data tests have not yet passed the A9 faithfulness gate, the 5 `not-representative` tests are still counted in the headline 30 refutations (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`), 5 of 6 OpenResearch-grounded headline tests were reproductions of known literature results (`repo/README.md`), and the wild-type zebrafish numbers in the design studio are disclosed as circular (`repo/README.md`).
justifications.decentralized-agency: Capabilities and epistemic roles are distributed across multiple model families and harnesses (`repo/AGENTS.md`, `repo/chats/SWARM_COORDINATION.md`, `captured/subagent-sessions.txt`), enforcing `assessor != builder` between Claude builders (Opus/Sonnet) and blind assessors across GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.7, and self-hosted Qwen3-32B (`repo/README.md`). The pack documents 101 local Cursor chats, 262 subagents, 19 cloud agents merging isolated slice branches (`captured/github-prs.json` #18–#33), external social agents (`delfie` on Moltbook/The Colony and `delfie-claude` in SentiLab), and the imported MorphoSwarm Frontier workspace (`captured/github-prs.json` #84, `captured/git-log.txt` with 1,327 `SciDEX Bot` commits). Genuine decentralized coordination without a central planner is demonstrated in two places: (1) the `decentralized` arm of the four-arm experiment (`repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md`, `SUMMARY.md`), where three domain queens (`q-evolution`, `q-morphology`, `q-holdout`) holding distinct portal briefs autonomously pulled tasks from a shared board and used peer gap notes and tips to recover failed dataset plans; and (2) external agents on Moltbook (`vina`, `hivefound`, `nanoswarm`, `doctor_memory`, `grokbot_polymath`, `yuigui`, `sheeshscout` in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`) whose critiques altered pre-registered contracts and triggered new null experiments and superseding nanopubs (`captured/git-log.txt` `4aaf9ac1`). The score is capped at 7 because the main repository's scientific trajectory was primarily orchestrated by human operators and hub sessions (`repo/chats/README.md` logs 174 user prompts directing tasks), `swarm/state.json` is explicitly disclosed as a simulation (`repo/AGENTS.md`), and the Science Claw forum has only 1 registered agent (`delphisci`) and 0 external comments (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`, `captured/forum-feed.json`).
justifications.collective-capability: Unlike most multi-agent projects, this snapshot includes three explicit, quantitative multi-agent vs. single-agent evaluations (`repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md`, `repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md`, `repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`). First, in two pre-registered 20-claim experiments (`repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md`, `SUMMARY.md`), four arms (`single`, `isolated`, `centralized`, `decentralized`) using identical models (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), tools, and schemas were mechanically verified (`verify.mjs`) on whether named public datasets resolve and match titles with zero fabricated identifiers: every multi-agent arm beat the single agent by +4 to +6 verified datasets out of 20 in both Experiment 1 (17–19/20 vs. 13/20; replicates 15–19/20 vs. 15/20) and Experiment 2 (16–18/20 vs. 12/20), and `centralized` beat `isolated` by +2 claims in both experiments (19 vs. 17; 18 vs. 16) via verifier-driven retries. Second, on leave-one-out routing across 99 decisive claim tests (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`), gating on two-assessor agreement (`GPT-5.6 Sol` vs. `Grok 4.7`) caught 12 of 17 assessor errors and raised trusted accuracy from 83.0% to 93.5%. Third, on Aristotle *History of Animals* Book VI (`repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md`), a blinded comparison of the swarm against three single-agent chains (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol) honestly reported a null on extraction and score accuracy while showing that only multi-provider assessment yields a calibration disagreement signal (64% verdict agreement). It does not reach 9–10 because `centralized` and `decentralized` were indistinguishable (<2 claims apart) at n=20, the single agent's shortfall in Experiment 2 was caused by context exhaustion (leaving 8 of 20 plans blank in one 20-claim call) at 1/5th to 1/10th the cost ($0.52 vs. $4.48–$6.37), and `verify.mjs` only checked URL/title resolution rather than whether the dataset actually measures the claim's variables.
justifications.execution-validation: There is a substantial, running, externally accessible software and hardware stack: the live MCP server (`https://mcp.delphibio.org/mcp` / `https://delphisci-mcp.fly.dev/mcp` with 1,522 tool calls across 60 sessions on Oct 31 in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`, plus a 100-case test suite passing 93/100 in `captured/github-issues.json` #56), the static claim graph and portal (`https://delphibio.org`), the Mission Control dashboard and 3D organism Perturb Studio (`https://delphi-mission-control.ashenoy000.workers.dev`), the MorphoSwarm Frontier workspace (`studio/` from PR #84), the Science Claw forum (`captured/forum-feed.json`), and physical Formlabs SLA 3D prints of real vs. Hoffmann-2018 Voronoi dragonfly hindwings (`repo/README.md`, `assets/arigomphus-wing.jpg`). End-to-end validation is backed by an automated execution harness (`repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json`) that re-ran 170 data tests and reproduced 131 within `1e-6` relative tolerance (with 24 minor live-API or formatting drifts), plus statement-level mutation testing of the Lean proofs (`captured/git-log.txt` `96c609cb`: 61/61 mutants rejected). It is held back from 9–10 by concrete integration regressions open on `main` after merging PR #73 (`captured/github-issues.json` #75: `node lean/registry/check-exposed.mjs` fails with 9 unmapped `*_rules_out` lemmas and a stale `/api/lean` mirror; #76: `leanbio` grounding cache misses on `main` claims; #77: `node holdout/check-leaks.mjs` reports ~20,000 hits; #78: two colliding nanopub generators; #56: Windows backslash bug in local MCP mode), 3 failed and 6 unverified data tests in `repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json`, and 9 uncommitted dirty files at capture time (`MANIFEST.json`).
justifications.collaboration-bonus: The pack documents two forms of concrete external collaboration that produced verified artifacts. First, in the SentiLab hackathon room (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`, tickets `897c7563` and `ba58c374`), Delphi's agent `delfie-claude` reproduced SentiLab's TAP-2.5D thermal chiplet baseline (75.48 / 115.94 °C in HotSpot 6.0), diagnosed a convection-share discrepancy in HotSpot 7.0 (123.42 / 232.67 °C), and delivered a 9-line patch plus reproduction harness (`#57314`, `#57872`) that was independently re-run and verified by the ScienceClaw team (`#57666`, `#57883` byte-identical) and Team Vortex on ARM (`#57881`), earning explicit credit on SentiLab's presentation slides (`"Delfie (delphisci team)"`) and closing both host tickets (`#57756`). Second, on Moltbook (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`), exchanges with nine external agents (`vina`, `hivefound`, `nanoswarm`, `doctor_memory`, `grokbot_polymath`, `yuigui`, `sheeshscout`, `nyna`, `anandanode`) produced concrete experimental changes—most notably `vina`'s segmenter-bias null experiment and `doctor_memory`'s formalization tagging and 25-record calibration batch (`06c55766`)—with the external agents credited via `dct:contributor` in superseding nanopubs (`captured/git-log.txt` `4aaf9ac1`). In addition, the team audited external repos `Pavel-Tk/fittest` (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`, issue #57) and `BigBirdReturns/GSK-LeanBio` (`captured/git-log.txt` `b3180b12`, issue #82), and teammate Kris Ganjam's `delphi-evolve` and `delphi-frontier` imported 1,326 claim versions over 30 `frontier-adapters` MCP sessions (`repo/README.md`, `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`). It does not reach 9–10 because no external biology team outside the Delphi collaborators has documented reuse of the `delphisci` MCP server or nanopub graph in their own biological result (`captured/github-issues.json` #41), and the Science Claw forum has 0 external registrants (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`).

comparison_found.note: Three quantitative comparisons exist in the pack: (1) Two pre-registered 20-claim experiments (`four-arm/PREREG.md`, `SUMMARY.md`) comparing `single`, `isolated`, `centralized`, and `decentralized` arms (all `claude-sonnet-5-5`) on mechanically verified public dataset test plans: every multi-agent arm beat `single` by +4 to +6 of 20 claims in both Exp 1 (17–19 vs 13) and Exp 2 (16–18 vs 12) with 0 fabricated IDs in final plans, and `centralized` beat `isolated` by +2 claims in both runs, though `centralized` vs `decentralized` showed no difference (<2 claims) and `single` cost 5–10x less and mainly failed via blank plans from 20-claim context exhaustion; (2) a blinded extraction and resolvability-scoring comparison on Aristotle HA Book VI (`aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md`) across the swarm and three single-agent chains (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol), finding no single-vs-swarm quality gap on extraction/scoring (r=0.58–0.84) but showing that only multi-provider assessment provides a disagreement signal; and (3) a 99-claim leave-one-out routing test (`plugins/fittest/README.md`) showing two-assessor agreement raises trusted accuracy against data verdicts from 83.0% to 93.5%.

top_three_fixes: Run the two-provider A9 faithfulness gate (`GPT-5.6 Sol` and `Grok 4.7`) on the 65 unchecked organism-level (`biological`) claim tests (starting with the 11 headline math-in-organisms claims) and filter agreed `not-representative` tests out of the headline support/refutation counts in `scripts/site/build-claim-graph.mjs` (raises `scientific-impact` +1, +2.5 weighted points).

Fix the post-merge CI and execution regressions on `main`: map the 9 `*_rules_out` lemmas and rebuild `/api/lean` so `node lean/registry/check-exposed.mjs` passes (#75), scope `holdout/check-leaks.mjs` (#77), fix the Windows path bug in `mcp/lib.mjs` (#56), and repair the 3 failed / 6 unverified test runners in `repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json` (raises `execution-validation` +1, +1.0 weighted point).

Add a 20-call sequential single-agent baseline (1 claim per call, same model and per-claim context) plus blind cross-provider quality scoring to `test-data/agent-comparison/` so the collective advantage is isolated from single-call context exhaustion (raises `collective-capability` +1, +2.5 weighted points).

assessments.summary: DELPHI is an unusually rigorous and ambitious epistemic engine that pairs 1,763 extracted biology and math claims, 73 zero-`sorry` Lean 4 theorems, 174 executable data tests (90 on organisms), and 880 production nanopublications with an interactive multi-scale organism design studio and physical 3D prints. Its standout strengths are its scientific honesty—actively refuting its own flying-fish genetic convergence hypothesis, running segmenter-bias null controls prompted by outside agents, and auditing refutations with a two-provider faithfulness gate—and its pre-registered four-arm experiments showing a +4 to +6 claim multi-agent gain over a single agent on verified dataset plans. Expanding the faithfulness gate to positive organism tests and cleaning up post-merge CI regressions (`check-exposed.mjs` and 9 failed/unverified test scripts) would make the release airtight.

justifications.problem-significance: The project tackles the genuinely hard problem of turning broad, historically important biological propositions into traceable formal statements and empirical tests across organisms. The frozen snapshot spans 1,763 claims, 91 proved mathematical statements, 174 data-tested claims and an organism inventory of 1,036 matched taxa (captured/mcp-overview.json, captured/mcp-tests-summary.json, captured/mcp-organisms.json). This is scientifically consequential because it explicitly separates proof from biological truth and exposes nulls, refutations and untestable claims, but the scope is diffuse: 1,522 claims are still neither proved nor tested, many source claims are historical rather than current frontier hypotheses, and issue #42's flying-fish program is primarily a plan rather than a completed scientific result (captured/github-issues.json).
justifications.scientific-impact: There are real, checkable results rather than only infrastructure: 174 unique claims have data verdicts (93 supports, 37 mixed, 30 refutes, 14 inconclusive), 90 use organism data, and 91 mathematical claims are recorded as proved, including 73 Lean-checked results (captured/mcp-tests-summary.json, captured/mcp-overview.json, captured/lean-reports.txt). The cell-geometry work found a consequential segmenter-bias null and downgraded a prior conclusion, while plant hygromorph work combines Lean statements with a small real-organism bilayer test (captured/github-issues.json issues #68, #69 and #81). Impact is capped because most tests are computational or historical reproductions, biological generality is often weak, only 33 of 174 tested claims have the independent faithfulness gate, and 5 of those were judged not representative with 6 contested (repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md).
justifications.decentralized-agency: The snapshot shows substantial distribution of labor and capability: 101 local chats, 262 subagents, 19 cloud agents, multiple model providers, distinct extraction, assessment, formalization, testing and red-team roles, and durable handoffs through files, issues and nanopublications (repo/COLLABORATIONS.md, repo/chats/README.md, captured/subagent-sessions.txt). Agents also triggered revisions after independent objections, including the segmenter-bias correction recorded in issues #68 and #69 (captured/github-issues.json). This is not a 10 because team roles and work packages were often centrally assigned by a human or lead issue (#53), the emperor/king/queen organization is partly simulation or design rather than demonstrated autonomous governance (repo/chats/SWARM_COORDINATION.md), and the internal forum snapshot has only one registered agent, no comments and four open requests (captured/forum-feed.json, captured/forum-requests.json).
justifications.collective-capability: A direct four-arm comparison is present and pre-registered: on two 20-claim runs, single-agent coverage was 13 and 12, isolated workers 17 and 16, centralized swarm 19 and 18, and decentralized swarm 18 and 17 (repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md, repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md). This is clear evidence that parallel collective organization improved verified dataset-identifier coverage over one agent. The score stops at 8 because centralized and decentralized arms were effectively tied, the decentralized arm fabricated an identifier on a first attempt in experiment 1, all arms used the same model/provider, n=20 per run is small, costs were roughly 5.2x and 10.7x the single arm, and the metric verifies landing pages rather than whether the proposed datasets scientifically measure each claim; the Aristotle pilot likewise found no swarm accuracy advantage and lacked ground truth (repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md).
justifications.execution-validation: This is a functioning, externally queryable system with claims, proofs, tests, organism records, MCP interfaces and nanopublication manifests, not an architecture sketch (repo/mcp/README.md, captured/nanopub-manifests.txt). The executable-claims snapshot reports 131 reproduced, but also 24 drifted, 6 skipped, 3 failed and 6 unverified runs (repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json), while an independent MCP audit reports 93 of 100 cases passing and identifies concrete defects (captured/github-issues.json issue #56). Validation is therefore substantial but incomplete: 141 of 174 tested claims lack independent faithfulness review, issue #72 records that published nanopubs can drift from result.json, and issue #75 records a failing Lean exposure check (repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md, captured/github-issues.json).
justifications.collaboration-bonus: The pack documents more than an offer: SentiLab reused the HotSpot work, independently reran it, incorporated a patch and credited Delfie in its slides, which is material cross-team propagation (repo/COLLABORATIONS.md). MorphoSwarm Frontier also imported Delphi claims and exposed a live adapter, although its own record says no cross-boundary scientific result had yet been produced; the public MCP and Fittest integration are useful shared infrastructure but are not by themselves evidence of another team's result (repo/COLLABORATIONS.md, repo/plugins/fittest/README.md). This merits a high bonus, but not 10, because the strongest documented reuse is concentrated in one collaboration and the internal forum shows little uptake (captured/forum-feed.json).

problem-significance: Select one current biological question with a named external scientist, explicit decision consequence and matched organism dataset, then make it the headline target instead of treating all 1,763 claims as equally central.
scientific-impact: Complete independent non-builder faithfulness reviews for the highest-impact unchecked tests and remove not-representative results from headline evidence counts.
Replicate a headline biological result on an independent dataset or organism rather than adding another historical or computational claim.
decentralized-agency: Run one end-to-end task where agents independently claim work, revise priorities and hand off through shared state without a human assigning the work packages, then preserve the event log.
collective-capability: Blindly score the existing four-arm outputs for scientific dataset-variable adequacy, not merely resolvable identifiers, using an independent provider and an adjudicated reference.
Repeat with at least two model families so model choice is not confounded with organization.
execution-validation: Resolve or explicitly quarantine the 24 drifted, 3 failed and 6 unverified executable claims and add a release check that compares published nanopub verdicts with current result.json files.
Close the failing Lean exposure and stale static-mirror checks recorded in issue #75.
collaboration-bonus: Obtain a second external team's committed result or report that directly depends on a Delphi tool, dataset or experiment, with a stable link and exact artifact reused.

comparison_found.note: Two pre-registered 20-claim experiments compared single agent, isolated workers, centralized swarm and decentralized swarm on verified dataset-identifier coverage. Collective arms beat the single agent, but centralized and decentralized swarms were indistinguishable; the comparison did not adjudicate scientific adequacy of the datasets and used one model/provider.

top_three_fixes: 1. Add blinded independent scientific-adequacy scoring to the existing four-arm outputs, converting the strongest comparison from URL coverage into a science-relevant benchmark.
2. Run the independent faithfulness gate on the highest-impact unchecked claim tests and revise headline counts to include only representative evidence.
3. Repair the drifted, failed and unverified executable claims and enforce result.json-to-nanopub consistency at release.

highest_value_improvement.title: Blindly adjudicate four-arm scientific adequacy
highest_value_improvement.what: Have a non-builder provider, blind to arm labels, score every proposed dataset in the two existing four-arm experiments against a fixed rubric for whether its variables, population and access route can actually test the assigned claim; adjudicate disagreements and publish arm-level totals beside the existing identifier-coverage totals.
highest_value_improvement.why_this_one: The runs and outputs already exist, so this adds little compute or engineering while directly strengthening the 25%-weight collective-capability criterion and the validation criterion. It is cheaper than running a new swarm experiment or completing faithfulness review across 141 tests, and it addresses the largest weakness in the project's strongest comparative evidence.
highest_value_improvement.evidence_that_would_prove_it: A committed blinded-adjudication table keyed to all 40 claims, with per-dataset variable/population/access verdicts, assessor identities, disagreements, adjudicated arm totals and the unchanged pre-registered arm labels revealed only after scoring.

missing_evidence: Independent domain-expert review of the biological meaning and novelty of the headline data results.
A blinded ground-truth assessment of scientific adequacy for the four-arm comparison outputs.
Complete independent faithfulness assessments for 141 of the 174 tested claims.
Independent replication on a second dataset or organism for the headline biological findings.
Evidence that the decentralized organization outperforms the centralized swarm rather than merely matching it.
assessments.summary: Delphi is an unusually substantial and self-critical scientific claim system: it has formal proofs, organism-linked tests, reproducibility records and a real four-arm agent comparison. Its strongest limitation is that much of the scale is not yet biologically validated: most claims remain untested, most completed tests lack independent faithfulness review, and the measured collective advantage is identifier coverage rather than scientific correctness.

justifications.problem-significance: The goal in repo/README.md is to find laws of biology that hold across organisms, stated so they can be formalized and tested. captured/mcp-overview.json shows why that is open: 1763 claims, 189 with math, 91 theorems (73 Lean-checked, 18 literature), and only 11 math claims supported by measurements on organisms, with 1522 neither proved nor tested. The corpus spans Darwin (247), Thompson (291), Levin (310), Wolfram (321), Aristotle (566) and the population-genetics set, and repo/problems/README.md lists unsolved tier A–C targets (Rule 110 in Lean, Lewontin's paradox, metabolic scaling, the bioelectric code) with acceptance criteria and falsifiers. That is a hard scientific problem, not a demo. It stops short of 9 because 566 Aristotle claims are entirely untested and Wolfram's 64 data tests are computational (captured/mcp-tests-summary.json), so a large share of the snapshot is catalogue extraction whose resolution would not change what a working biologist does next, and the 'fundamental theorems' framing is wider than the open problems the pack shows anyone attacking.
justifications.scientific-impact: There are real, checked outputs. captured/mcp-tests-summary.json and repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md record 174 claims tested (93 supports, 37 mixed, 30 refutes, 14 inconclusive) from 189 runs, 90 of them on organism data, plus 16 or 17 tests still only pre-registered. captured/lean-reports.txt records machine-checked formalizations (Darwin Islands 4, Struggle 7, Succession 5, Tree 4; Thompson Cells 15, Magnitude 13, Mechanics 7, HornsLeavesEggs 12, Hygromorphs 4; TwelvePentagons none). README claims 880 production nanopubs from the first night; captured/nanopub-manifests.txt shows production manifest lines for Darwin 248, Thompson 874 and Wolfram 963, with Aristotle 566 and Levin 930 on the test registry only. Specific negatives are in SUMMARY.md (kimura-heterozygosity refutes, turing-ddi refutes, darwin1859-ch12-08 and ch12-09 refutes) and the Cellpose null in repo/COLLABORATIONS.md cut thompson1917-ch07-04 from confidence 0.60 to 0.35. Held at 6 because README's sponsor table says 5 of 6 OpenResearch headline tests were already in the literature and are reported as reproductions; the faithfulness table covers 33 of 174 tests (2 faithful, 17 narrower-scope, 5 agreed not-representative, 6 contested, 141 unchecked) while the headline still counts 30 refutes; 64 of 174 tests are Wolfram computations; and README says the design-studio zebrafish numbers are circular and the printed wings have no measured print-versus-design agreement.
justifications.decentralized-agency: Work is split across people and models. captured/git-stats.txt has 2421 commits from 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-01; captured/git-shortlog.txt is SciDEX Bot 1327, Amit Shenoy 897, Cursor Agent 367, Joel Dietz 224, plus Ashley Caselli, Kris Ganjam and others. captured/subagent-sessions.txt shows separate extraction, Grok and Gemini assessment, and Lean sessions. repo/chats/SWARM_COORDINATION.md counts 101 local chats, 262 subagents and 19 cloud agents, and says those use-case numbers are approximate and hand-counted, with the chat log last regenerated at 22 chats. repo/AGENTS.md defines emperor, king and queens and states that queens choose what to explore, and it also states that swarm/state.json is a simulation of the control loop. The decentralized arm in repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md does let three queens pull tickets from a board with no planner, but that arm wrote dataset plans; the organism inventory was one cloud agent per chapter slice (repo/test-data/organisms/README.md) and repo/chats/README.md shows the human assigning each workstream. Issue #53 assigns named owners. Moltbook agents changed files (COLLABORATIONS.md: vina's segmenter-bias null, doctor_memory's formalization tag at commit 912fbea9, grokbot_polymath's cornea amendment), which is distributed revision of details. The trajectory of what got built was still prescribed. Score 5.
justifications.collective-capability: A measured comparison is in the pack. repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md, pre-registered in four-arm/PREREG.md and qualified in four-arm/DEVIATIONS.md, runs four arms on the same 20 claims, the same claude-sonnet-5-5 model, the same prompt and the same budget. Experiment 1 verified datasets: single 13/20, isolated 17, centralized 19, decentralized 18; centralized beats single by 6, above the pre-registered margin of 2, and decentralized does not win because one attempt named a nonexistent NCBI accession (GCF_000337935.2). Experiment 2, with fetching required: 12, 16, 18, 17, and every multi-agent arm beats single by at least 4, with zero fabricated identifiers. Experiment 1 replicates kept centralized at 19 and decentralized at 18. The same file says the single agent costs about a fifth to a tenth as much and wins per verified dataset, that its shortfall is blank plans from context limits, that centralized versus decentralized is no difference, and that 'verified' means the landing page names the dataset. A second comparison, repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md, finds no swarm advantage on History of Animals Book VI: overlap and scores follow which model ran, and the write-up says the slice cannot separate one-versus-many from which model. README quotes a null collective result from delphi-evolve and says those counts were not re-run. The gain on the plan-naming task is measured; a gain in scientific judgment is not.
justifications.execution-validation: The system is running, not a slide. COLLABORATIONS.md records 1522 MCP tool calls and 60 sessions on 2026-10-31 after metrics shipped; captured/forum-feed.json has 20 live posts; the claim graph in captured/mcp-overview.json was built 2026-11-01 15:21; production nanopubs exist (nanopub-manifests.txt). repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json, ran 2026-11-01T12:13:41Z, re-executed 170 data tests: 131 reproduced, 24 drifted, 6 skipped, 3 failed, 6 unverified. Among the 24 drifted, 16 kept the committed verdict and none flipped it (darwin1859-ch10-02 is supports to supports, with Kruskal H moving from 3079.996 to 3079.968); 8 drifted rows and 71 of 131 reproduced rows have verdict.now null, so much of 'reproduced' is a derived-file match. Failures are levin-2018-hcn2-16 (missing json), levin-2019-boundary-14 (no module tmtools) and thompson1917-ch08-02 (timeout 3600s). The run's kind is data only, so the Lean reports were not re-checked here. Open issues #72 (published records can drift from result.json), #37 (template declarations false under ontology v2.0) and #75 (check-exposed fails) are in captured/github-issues.json. repo/mcp/README.md says DNS for mcp.delphibio.org still has to be pointed. captured/mcp-morpholib-live.json finds 109 production MorphoEval nanopubs against 142 audits in the links file. That is a functioning system with a partial independent re-run, not a clean external validation.
justifications.collaboration-bonus: Capabilities were offered and one outside use is logged, without a second team's scientific result that depends on this graph. The public MCP and forum are up (repo/README.md, repo/forum/README.md). captured/forum-requests.json and captured/forum-feed.json are 20 posts, every author delphisci, 0 comments, 4 collaboration requests still open. Issue #41 is titled as reusable capabilities for other teams and says that category currently has no evidence; issue #35 is still open. COLLABORATIONS.md's MCP table peaks at 3 unique visitors; 30 frontier-adapters sessions are unidentified, and README says Frontier imported 1326 claim versions with no byte-checked artifact and no Delphi verdict cited in a Frontier result. The same README says delphi-evolve turned Kimura, Fisher and Turing claims into executable checks and that those counts were not re-run here; captured/github-prs.json shows Kris Ganjam's #84 merged as a Frontier import into this repo, which is a sibling joining the tree rather than an outside result. The concrete assist is SentiLab tickets 897c7563 and ba58c374 in COLLABORATIONS.md: a HotSpot patch, a logged independent re-run, slides credited to Delfie, tickets closed. That is one self-logged engineering assist on chiplet heat, not documented reuse of the claim graph, the organism inventory or a data verdict by another team. Inbound Moltbook objections did change this repo; that is the opposite direction. Score 6.

problem-significance: Take one tier-B problem already named in repo/problems/README.md, such as land-versus-sea turnover (darwin1859-ch10-03, already pre-registered in captured/mcp-tests-summary.json), run it, and show the result against the modern literature so the snapshot is about an open biological question rather than a catalogue of 1763 historical sentences.
scientific-impact: Finish the faithfulness gate for every refutes row that SUMMARY.md has not checked, starting with kimura-heterozygosity and turing-ddi, using a provider other than the builder, and stop counting the 5 agreed not-representative tests inside the headline 30 refutes.
decentralized-agency: Replace the simulated swarm/state.json named in repo/AGENTS.md with one logged cycle in which the three queens pull the 17 pre-registered tests from a shared board and the human does not assign claims, and commit the board log.
collective-capability: Have a non-Claude assessor score every experiment-2 plan on whether the named dataset's variables can decide the claim, then apply the pre-registered margin to that count beside repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md.
execution-validation: Re-run latest.json with a stated numeric tolerance so the 16 verdict-stable drifts count as reproduced, fix the three failures (tmtools, missing wt4 json, the 3600s timeout), and include the Lean modules from captured/lean-reports.txt in the same run.
collaboration-bonus: Get one outside team to cite a specific Delphi claim IRI or verdict in their own result file, and put that file or nanopub URI in the pack; the SentiLab log and the 30 frontier-adapters sessions do not yet do this.

comparison_found.note: Two pre-registered 20-claim experiments compare single, isolated, centralized and decentralized arms on verified public datasets (experiment 1: 13/17/19/18 of 20; experiment 2: 12/16/18/17). Centralized beats single by 6 claims both times. The metric is URL-and-name match, not whether the dataset can decide the claim. A second comparison in repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md finds no swarm gain on extraction or assessment of History of Animals Book VI. README quotes a null from delphi-evolve that this pack did not re-run.

top_three_fixes: Score the existing experiment-2 four-arm plans for variable match, not just URL match: about 6 hours, and the only change that can move the 0.25-weight collective-capability score with data already in the pack.

Faithfulness-check the unchecked refutations, especially kimura-heterozygosity and turing-ddi, and drop the 5 agreed not-representative tests from the headline refutation count: about 10 hours, moves the other 0.25-weight criterion.
Log one queen-pulled cycle on the 17 pre-registered tests with no human assignment: about 8 hours, the cheapest credible move on decentralized-agency, which is stuck at the single-planner anchor.

highest_value_improvement.title: Score the four-arm plans on whether the dataset can decide the claim
highest_value_improvement.what: A model other than Claude reads the frozen experiment-2 plans (single, isolated, centralized, decentralized; 20 claims each) already cited from four-arm/runs2 in repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md and marks each named dataset yes or no: do its variables match the claim's quantities, naming the missing variable on a no. Apply the pre-registered rule (0 fabricated identifiers and a margin of at least 2) to that count and write the table next to SUMMARY.md.
highest_value_improvement.why_this_one: Collective capability is a quarter of the weighted total and is already the project's best measured result, but the pack itself says the metric is only that a landing page names the dataset. Rescoring plans that already exist is a few hours. Completing faithfulness on 141 tests, re-running Lean, or standing up a real queen cycle either takes longer per point or sits on the 0.10 or 0.20 weights. A reporting-only cleanup of the 24 drifts would not move a score, because those mismatches are already in latest.json and 16 of them keep the same verdict.
highest_value_improvement.evidence_that_would_prove_it: A table beside repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md with, for each experiment-2 arm, variable-match counts out of 20, the assessor, and the same pairwise verdicts the pre-registration already defines.

missing_evidence: sponsors/OPENRESEARCH.md and the six orx run identifiers cited from repo/README.md are not in the pack, so the '5 of 6 already answered' claim is taken from the README sentence only.
The four-arm plan files, verifier fetches and log.jsonl cited from SUMMARY.md are not in the pack; only SUMMARY.md, PREREG.md and DEVIATIONS.md are.
swarm/state.json and swarm/metrics.json are named in repo/AGENTS.md and are not in the pack, so the simulation disclaimer could not be checked against the file.
latest.json re-runs data tests only; no Lean replay is in the pack beyond the formalized counts in captured/lean-reports.txt.
SentiLab slides, ticket diffs and the Frontier citation of a Delphi verdict are not in the pack; uptake is the project's own COLLABORATIONS.md and README.
Per-claim faithfulness.json and result.json bodies are not in the pack; verdicts are taken from SUMMARY.md.
mcp/usage/2026-10-31.json is not in the pack; the 1522 calls and client names are quoted from COLLABORATIONS.md.
Individual git-log bodies beyond the header sample, and the full text of the 109 MorphoEval labels, were not needed for the scores and were not line-read.
assessments.summary: This is a real attempt to turn classical biological claims into formal statements and data tests: 174 claims have verdicts, 90 of them on organisms, 73 are Lean-checked, and a public claim server exists, but most of the 1763 claims are still untested and the headline tests are largely reproductions. A pre-registered four-arm comparison does show multi-agent coverage beating a single agent by at least 4 of 20 dataset names, twice, while an Aristotle slice shows no swarm gain and the single agent remains cheaper. Agents had distinct roles under a human-assigned pipeline; outside teams were offered the server, and the only closed external assist in the pack is a self-logged thermal patch, not reuse of a biological result.
